tweets.text:
Cleaning up meeting notes. Putting in the time to run a great activity. Sending a link to the one-pager folder two days in advance of the workshop. Doing the pre-read. Taking good notes. Writing the weekly recap.

These are the "boring bits" of product ... 1/n

These are the boring bits that busy people often don't have time for.

It's crazy lately!

Who needs that bureaucratic bullshit?

"Excuse me ... I'm working on the strategy..."

Ugh...PROCESS!

2/n

This work often goes under-appreciated + unrewarded.

And in some cases ridiculed and diminished.

But while tactics (and org culture) vary, most effective teams figure how how to make (some amount of) it happen.

3/n

Example: a coworker who used to dedicate one full our of prep PER ATTENDEE when it came to important meetings like kickoffs.

To many that is a waste.

But no joke…the return on investment was huge.

4/n

Yeah, the strategy was great, but have you ever shown up for a series of well designed meetings with clear action items and pre-reads?

Next week... show some appreciation for the people doing the "boring" parts of product in your org.

And if that's you...thank you!

5/end
